To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of an ontologically sound conceptual model of things and properties improves users' understanding of a domain.

(a) users of conceptual models can understand a domain better using an ontologically sound model than using an alternative model that is not ontologically sound, and (b) users of conceptual model can understand a domain just as well using an ontologically model that is not sound as using an ontologically unsound model that has the same number of entities and relationships.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How do the representations of things and their properties affect the understanding of the domain by conceptual modelling users?
how the representation of things affects the understanding of conceptual models.
the representation of things, properties and relations in conceptual modelling and with the use of ontological theory to inform conceptual modelling practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ontologically sound representation was the best of the three representations in terms of the users' ability to understand the domain and that the ER representation was better than the ORM representation.

the distinction between things and property is an important distinction in conceptual modelling; the distinction between things that are and properties that are not things is an important distinction; and the distinction between things whose existence is independent of their properties, and properties whose existence depends on their things, is an important distinction.
the representation of things as objects and properties as relationships in the conceptual model of a domain is a better way of representing the domain than alternative approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ontologically sound representation is the most effective representation of things and property in conceptual modelling.
we have shown that the use of ontological theory can improve our conceptual modelling practice.
ontologically sound representations are better representations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ontological theory can be used to support the design of conceptual modelling languages.
the distinction between things and property is important and should be made explicit.
conceptual modelling should be based on sound ontological theory.
